research_rationale: EO 10559 (Sept. 8, 1954; 19 FR 5879) has two operative sections: sec. 1 delegates to the Budget Director the President's authority to allocate the 'Expenses of Management Improvement' appropriation (and any reenactment); sec. 2 requires reports and direction of the funded activities. No amendment of EO 10559 is recorded in the OFR catalog edges or the 1989 Codification disposition table ('Superseded by EO 11230'). EO 11230 sec. 2(2) expressly supersedes EO 10559; EO 11230 states no effective date and so took effect on issuance, June 28, 1965. Both clauses therefore first ended on 1965-06-28, which is also the whole-order end. Savings: EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps prior actions and regulations in effect under EO 11230 and sec. 3(b) redirects references; the function itself passes to EO 11230 sec. 1(23). research_rationale: EO 10836 (Sept. 8, 1959; 24 FR 7269) amends section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 by substituting paragraph (l) (approvals under section 11 of the Act of June 6, 1924, as renumbered and amended in 1952) and adding paragraph (o) (Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 44(a) transitional grants and sec. 44(b) interim services and fund allocation). Neither clause carries an expiry. The statutory life of the Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 44 grant authority was not checked against the Statutes at Large (not held in the project); EO 11230 sec. 1(26) re-delegated the same sec. 44(a) and 44(b) authorities on June 28, 1965, which indicates they were still treated as live, so no earlier statutory lapse is asserted. The OFR catalog and the 1989 Codification ('Amended EO 10530 ... Superseded by EO 11230') show no other later event. EO 11230 sec. 2 supersedes Part I of EO 10530 (item 1) and EO 10836 (item 6), effective on issuance June 28, 1965. All clauses first ended on 1965-06-28, the whole-order end. The only current-law hit is the 3 U.S.C. 301 note's status line for EO 10530 ('as amended by ... Ex. Ord. No. ...'), an amendment history of the host order, not a current predicate for this order; the provisions it added to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 were superseded with Part I by EO 11230 sec. 2(1).

research_rationale: EO 10889 (Oct. 5, 1960; 25 FR 9633) adds paragraphs (p), (q) and (r) to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 and, in sec. 2, supersedes four 1960 presidential letters under Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 45(a). Clause by clause: (p)(1), the determination power under sec. 45(a), ran until EO 11164 substituted the whole of paragraph (p) on Aug. 1, 1964 (EO 11164 states no effective date; effective on issuance). (p)(2), the conveyance power, was delegated only 'until July 1, 1964' by this order's own words, so it first ended on 1964-07-01 by its own terms, before EO 11164 restored a conveyance power without that limit. (q) was replaced in full by EO 10960 on Aug. 21, 1961 (substitution 'to read as follows', effective on issuance). Sec. 2's supersession of the four letters was completed on issuance, Oct. 5, 1960 (spent; recorded as its first end). (r) and the enacting words continued until EO 11230 sec. 2 superseded Part I of EO 10530 (item 1) and EO 10889 (item 7), effective on issuance June 28, 1965. Convention: a clause whose whole text is replaced by a later order's substituted text ends on that order's effective date; the substituted text is the later order's clause. A first_end that is a limit in the order itself uses the first day the clause no longer applied. Whole-order end = latest clause end = 1965-06-28. The OFR catalog also records EO 10960 as amending this order; the 1989 Codification row reads 'Amended EO 10530. Amended by EO 10960 ... Superseded by EO 11230'. The only current-law hit is the 3 U.S.C. 301 note's status line for EO 10530 ('as amended by ... Ex. Ord. No. ...'), an amendment history of the host order, not a current predicate for this order; the provisions it added to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 were superseded with Part I by EO 11230 sec. 2(1). The clause inventory is quoted from the official FR scan (the draft's clauses came from a mirror transcription and were not used).

research_rationale: EO 8546 (Sept. 24, 1940; 5 FR 3817-3818) creates the Defense Communications Board (para. 1), gives it planning functions for national emergencies (para. 2), sets its chairmanship and secretary (para. 3), its scope and broadcasting studies (para. 4), committees (paras. 5-6), consultation (para. 7), the advisory role of the Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee during war or national emergency (para. 8) and reporting to the President (para. 9). Later events: EO 8960 (Dec. 6, 1941) substituted the Treasury officer named in paras. 1 and 3; EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) renamed the Board the Board of War Communications and amended this order accordingly; neither ended a clause (word substitutions; the clauses continue as amended). EO 8964 and EO 9089 gave the Board further powers without amending this order. The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 (Feb. 24, 1947; 12 FR 1363) para. 1 abolishes the Board, created 'as the Defense Communications Board by Executive Order No. 8546', and para. 2 revokes EO 8546; it states no effective date, so it took effect on issuance. Every clause therefore first ended on 1947-02-24, the whole-order end. The two current-law hits (47 U.S.C. 606 note) print EO 9831 itself, which confirms the abolition and revocation; no current predicate. The 1989 Codification row: 'Amended by EOs 8960, 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'.

research_rationale: EO 8964 (Dec. 10, 1941; 6 FR 6367-6368) directs the Defense Communications Board to exercise the President's Communications Act sec. 606 powers over radio stations (enacting words) under eleven regulations (allocation plans, designation and classes of stations for government use or closure, agency reporting, limits, continued private operation, just compensation, relinquishment, priority of communications, definitions, publication). None has its own expiry; para. 8 lets the Board relinquish control case by case, which ends particular uses, not the clauses. EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) renamed the Board and amended this order accordingly (no clause ended). The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 para. 2 revokes EO 8964, effective on issuance Feb. 24, 1947; every clause and the order first ended on 1947-02-24. Counterevidence: the current-law hit (47 U.S.C. 606 note) states that EO 8964 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 9831, eff. Feb. 24, 1947', confirming the date. 1989 Codification: 'Amended by EO 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'.

research_rationale: EO 9089 (Mar. 6, 1942; 7 FR 1777-1778) directs the Defense Communications Board to exercise the President's Communications Act sec. 606(d) powers over wire communication facilities (enacting words) under ten regulations parallel to EO 8964's radio regulations. Sec. 606(d), as quoted in the order, runs 'during the period ending not later than six months after the termination of such state or threat of war' or an earlier date set by concurrent resolution; the state of war had not been terminated by Feb. 24, 1947 and no such concurrent resolution is recorded in the bounded sources, so the statutory period had not run. EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) renamed the Board and amended this order accordingly. The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 para. 2 revokes EO 9089, effective on issuance Feb. 24, 1947; every clause and the order first ended on 1947-02-24. 1989 Codification: 'Amended by EO 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'. No current-law citation. The draft's clause text quoted the footnote-joined number of EO 8546 (read as a non-existent order); the quotation is now split around it.

research_rationale: EO 9386 (Oct. 15, 1943, effective Nov. 1, 1943; 8 FR 14103-14105) prescribes under sec. 10 of the Pay Readjustment Act of 1942 the daily allowances for quarters and subsistence of enlisted men not furnished them in kind (Section I with paragraphs A, B, four exceptions, C and two notes), travel allowances (Section II), advance payment (Section III) and quarters allowances for enlisted men of the first three grades with dependents (Section IV), and supersedes EO 9206 as amended. It has no expiry of its own. Later events: EO 9561 (effective June 1, 1945, term later extended by EO 9744C to June 30, 1947) temporarily raised one subsistence rate in paragraph A and Exception No. 1 (clauses continue as amended); EO 9825 substituted the whole of Section II effective Feb. 15, 1947, so the original Section II first ended on 1947-02-15 (convention: wholesale substitution ends the original clause; the new text is EO 9825's own clause). The supersession of EO 9206 was completed on Nov. 1, 1943 (spent). All other clauses ran until EO 9871, which 'shall supersede Executive Order No. 9386 ... as amended by Executive Order No. 9561 ... and shall be effective from July 1, 1947'. EO 9871 was signed July 8, 1947; following its stated effective date the clauses first ended on 1947-07-01, the whole-order end. The OFR catalog edges and the 1989 Codification ('Amended by EOs 9561, 9825 ... Superseded by EO 9871') show no other event. The 1946 amendments of the Pay Readjustment Act (60 Stat. 853, 858, cited by EO 9871) were not checked against the Statutes at Large (not held); EO 9825 still amended this order in January 1947 and EO 9871 superseded it 'as amended', which indicates it remained the operative regulation until then. No current-law citation. The draft had no clause inventory; it is built here from the official FR scan.

Section II of Executive Order No. 9386, 
dated October 15, 1943, prescribing al­
lowances for quarters and subsistence to 
enlisted men not furnished quarters or 
rations in kind, is hereby amended, eflec-, 
tive as of February 15, 1947, to read as 
follows:
S ection  II
Men traveling on duty including de­
tentions not exceeding thirty-one days 
at any one place, when not furnished 
sleeping car, stateroom accommodations, 
o r other quarters, and rations in kind, 
shall be granted a daily allowance of 
$5.00: Provided, that when quarters in 
kind are furnished, they shall be entitled 
only to an allowance for subsistence at 
the rate of $1.00 per meal, and when 
subsistence is furnished they shall be 
entitled only to an allowance for quar­
ters at the rate of $2.00 per day; except 
that, where travel is performed by rail 
or water, the allowance for subsistence 
shall be $1.25 for each meal required to 
be taken in a dining car on a train or in 
a dining room on a steamer, and If 
quarters are not provided for the day 
of such travel, the allowance for. quar­
ters shall be $1.75 when an allowance for 
subsistence is so furnished for one meal, 
$1.50 when an allowance for subsistence 
is so furnished for two meals, or $1.25 
when an allowance for subsistence is so 
furnished for three meals. For the pur­
poses of this section, quarters in kind will 
be considered as furnished for the day 
of arrival at a permanent station.
Men absent under orders from their 
station upon duty which involves travel 
and also temporary detentions during 
the journey shail be deemed to be trav­
eling under orders during the entire pe­
riod of such absence including the day 
of departure therefrom and return there­
to. For periods of detention in excess of 
thirty-one days at any one place, the 
allowances preseribed in Section I shall 
govern after the thirty-first day.

research_rationale: EO 11112 (June 12, 1963; 28 FR 6037-6038) establishes the President's Advisory Council on the Arts: establishment (1(a)), composition and terms (1(b)), chairman (1(c)), compensation (1(d)), meetings (1(e)), functions (2(a)(1)-(5)), hearing interested parties (2(b)), definition of the arts (2(c)), and agency liaison, information, assistance and GSA services (3(a)-(d)). No expiry or condition. EO 11124 (Oct. 28, 1963) substituted a new subsection (b) of Section 1 (two more ex officio members, up to forty private members), so the original 1(b) first ended on 1963-10-28 (convention: wholesale substitution ends the original clause; the new text is EO 11124's own clause). The National Council on the Arts Act of Sept. 3, 1964 did not itself abolish the Council; EO 11208 recites that it 'obviat[ed] the need' and then revokes EO 11112 and EO 11124, effective on issuance Mar. 24, 1965 (signature date garbled in the OCR; filing line Mar. 25, 1965 and OFR catalog Mar. 24, 1965). All other clauses first ended on 1965-03-24, the whole-order end. Whether private members were appointed before the Council's work was overtaken by the 1964 statute was not established from the bounded sources; the clauses' legal operation (the Council existed from the order, with ex officio federal members by office, and EO 11124 sec. 2 refers to sitting members) ran to the revocation, and no earlier presidential or statutory act ending the Council was found in the OFR catalog or the saved texts. 1989 Codification row: 'Amended by EO 11124 ... research_rationale: EO 9981 (July 26, 1948; 13 FR 4313) declares the President's policy of equality of treatment and opportunity in the armed services without regard to race, color, religion or national origin (para. 1) and creates the President's Committee on Equality of Treatment and Opportunity in the Armed Services with its powers, agency cooperation, testimony and duration (paras. 2-6). The clause inventory is quoted from the official FR scan. The only formal ending found is EO 11051 sec. 604(1) (Sept. 27, 1962), which supersedes and revokes EO 9981 'To the extent that [it has] not heretofore been made or become inapplicable' (1989 Codification: 'Revoked by EO 11051').
